definition: How much better an action was than the policy's average at that state (Q minus V).
details: How much better an action was than the policy's average at that state (Q minus V). Generalized Advantage Estimation is the standard bias-variance-controlled estimator; GRPO replaces learned value baselines with group-relative advantages.

explainer.lead: Advantage tells an agent whether a particular choice beat what its policy would usually do in the same situation. Comparing an action with that baseline gives learning a clearer signal than looking at the action’s outcome alone.

tiers.eli5: Imagine you usually score 70 on a quiz, but a new way of studying helps you score 80. The advantage of that choice is 10 points: it worked better than your usual approach. A score of 60 would have an advantage of minus 10, meaning it worked worse.
tiers.practitioner: Compute advantage as A(s, a) = Q(s, a) − V(s), keeping the action-specific value separate from the policy’s state baseline. GAE is the standard estimator when you want to control the bias–variance trade-off; GRPO instead uses group-relative advantages rather than learned value baselines. Do not treat GAE as a different advantage definition or a group-relative score as a learned V(s).
tiers.paperLevel: For policy π, the advantage is A^π(s, a) = Q^π(s, a) − V^π(s), so positive values indicate actions above the policy’s average at that state and negative values indicate actions below it. Generalized Advantage Estimation estimates this quantity with a controlled bias–variance trade-off. GRPO replaces learned value baselines with group-relative advantages.

explainer.example: At a particular state, an action has Q = 8, while the policy’s average value there is V = 5. Its advantage is 8 − 5 = 3, so the action is 3 units better than the policy’s average; an action with Q = 4 would instead have advantage −1.

usedIn.name: Generalized Advantage Estimation
usedIn.detail: Estimates advantages while controlling the trade-off between bias and variance.

usedIn.name: GRPO
usedIn.detail: Uses group-relative advantages instead of learned value baselines.

usedIn.name: Reinforcement learning
usedIn.detail: Scores an action relative to the policy’s average value in the same state.

explainer.intuition: A good outcome is not necessarily a good choice if every choice would have done just as well. Advantage removes the policy’s usual performance at that state, leaving the action’s relative contribution.
howItWorks: Start with a state and an action taken there.
Estimate Q(s, a), the value of that specific action.
Estimate V(s), the policy’s average value at that state.
Subtract V(s) from Q(s, a) to obtain the advantage.
Estimate the quantity with GAE, or use group-relative advantages in GRPO.
explainer.whyItMatters: Advantage separates an action’s relative merit from how favourable the state already was. GAE provides a standard bias–variance-controlled way to estimate it, while GRPO offers a group-relative alternative without a learned value baseline.
misconceptions: Advantage is not Q itself; it is Q minus V.
GAE is an estimator of advantage, not a different definition of it.
GRPO’s group-relative advantages do not use a learned value baseline.

diagram.caption: Advantage compares an action-specific value with the policy’s average value at the same state.
